decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with vertical through contacts build directly on the firm's core structuring and bonding know-how and fit its announced move toward multifunctional packaging wafers, so the sunk investment and strategic centrality favor keeping them.

Carrier wafers for handling smaller-diameter wafers were publicly announced, cost little to maintain alongside the established offer, and match the stated push into reusable carriers and thin-wafer handling.

The Cu-interposer technology was launched visibly at SEMICON Europa 2019 and represents substantial R&D investment central to the packaging-wafer direction, so management would attribute any slow uptake to the pandemic and keep it.

The Wafer Universe brand was publicly founded as a dedicated off-the-shelf channel and is cheap to sustain, so management would persist with it even if sales are modest, though it could be folded back into the main offer.

Glass-based circuit boards lie furthest from the core business and carry the greatest risk of being dropped, but the R&D already invested and the plausible claim that slow demand reflects a temporary market phase lead management to keep them for now.
